sections.heading: 1. The Cell
points: The **cell** is the **basic structural and functional unit of life** — the smallest unit that can carry out life processes.
Discovered by **Robert Hooke (1665)** in cork; living cells first seen by **Leeuwenhoek**.
**Cell theory** (Schleiden & Schwann; Virchow): all living things are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of life; and **new cells arise from pre-existing cells**.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Cells
points: **Prokaryotic cells** — no true **nucleus** or membrane-bound organelles (e.g. **bacteria**); DNA lies free.
**Eukaryotic cells** — have a **true nucleus** and membrane-bound organelles (plants, animals, fungi).
Organisms may be **unicellular** (Amoeba) or **multicellular** (humans, plants).

sections.heading: 3. Cell Structure and Organelles
points: **Plasma membrane** — selectively permeable; controls entry/exit (osmosis, diffusion).
**Cell wall** — rigid outer layer of **cellulose** (in **plant** cells only).
**Nucleus** — controls activities; contains **chromosomes (DNA/genes)**.
**Cytoplasm** — jelly-like fluid holding organelles.

sub: **Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, ribosomes (protein synthesis), lysosomes ('suicide bags'), vacuoles** (large in plant cells).

sections.heading: 4. Plant vs Animal Cell; Transport
points: **Plant cells** have a **cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole**; **animal cells** do not.
**Diffusion** — movement of substances from high to low concentration.
**Osmosis** — movement of **water** across a semi-permeable membrane (hypotonic/isotonic/hypertonic solutions).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Cell = basic unit of life; Robert Hooke (1665, cork); cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow).
Prokaryotes (bacteria, no true nucleus) vs eukaryotes (true nucleus + organelles).
Cell wall (cellulose) = plants only; nucleus controls the cell (DNA/chromosomes).
Mitochondria = powerhouse; chloroplast = photosynthesis; ribosomes = protein synthesis; lysosomes = 'suicide bags'.
Plant cell = wall + chloroplast + large vacuole; osmosis = water movement across a membrane.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Prokaryotes lack a true (membrane-bound) nucleus**; **eukaryotes have one**.
The **cell wall (cellulose)** is found **only in plant cells**.
**Mitochondria = powerhouse**; **chloroplast = photosynthesis** — don't swap.
**Osmosis** is the movement of **water** (not any substance) across a semi-permeable membrane.
